grand_strategy.reading:
The State of Palestine is a state whose government cannot protect its people, finance itself or even hold an election, and it knows it: its grand strategy is the strategy of staying in
the picture. Everything Ramallah does is a bet that the Palestinian question will be settled by others and that whoever is still standing, with a flag, a seat at the UN and a legal
personality, will be handed what is left. That produces the Luttwak pattern in its sharpest form: the means that keep the Authority alive (coordination with Israel, endorsement of the
Trump plan, reform pledges to donors, a managed succession) are the same that drain its credibility with Palestinians, while the means that raise its standing abroad (157 recognitions, the
ICJ opinion, the ICC) are punished with the loss of money and travel. In 2025-26 the pressure came from three sides at once: Israel's fiscal strangulation and settlement drive (UN: 'the PA
is at the brink of collapse'), a US-designed Gaza order that includes technocrats but not the Authority, and Hamas, which is losing public support (24%) but not its arms. The Western wave of
recognition in September 2025 and the settlement-goods bans of 2026 are real, but they give the Authority diplomatic oxygen, not territory or revenue. Two signals that are not rows: Abbas telling
the UN on 24 Sep 2026 that elections were on and postponing them sixteen days later, and the US ban that again kept him out of New York. With Israeli elections on 27 Oct 2026, the PA's real
question is whether a new government in Jerusalem would unfreeze the clearance revenues or whether the money, not the flag, decides its survival.

stances.note: Decided from the evidence: rival, not adversary. The PLO accepts Israel and the two-state outcome (Abbas to the UN, 24 Sep 2026: a two-state solution on international law) and the PA still lives inside the Oslo security and customs architecture, so it does not seek Israel's destruction; the coordination it has never fully ended (Arab Center: dense, and kept going through earlier suspensions) is the opposite of an adversary's posture. The hostility is real and one-sided in intent: the occupation (ICJ 2024: unlawful), the withholding of clearance revenues since May 2025, the E1 tenders of Aug 2026, the first Area A land seizure for settlements, settler violence at record levels (UN: about 1,430 incidents to 10 Aug 2026), and, per PISM, a coalition aim of blocking statehood and, if the far right wins, dismantling the PA. Israel's own grade of the PA may be harsher (build will flag the asymmetry if Jerusalem's card says adversary). No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Cooling: the Israeli election of 27 Oct 2026 is contested by blocs most of which oppose a Palestinian state (Al Jazeera). Bond - grievance: occupation, 1948 and 1967.
